front_blocks.md: Define **black body**.

back_blocks.md: A **black body** is an object that absorbs (or emits) all of the radiation incident on it, and does not reflect or transmit any radiation.

cards.back_md: A **black body** is an object that absorbs (or emits) all of the radiation incident on it, and does not reflect or transmit any radiation.

front_blocks.md: Define **black body radiation**.

back_blocks.md: **Black body radiation** is the thermal radiation emitted by all objects, in the form of electromagnetic waves, due to their temperature.

cards.back_md: **Black body radiation** is the thermal radiation emitted by all objects, in the form of electromagnetic waves, due to their temperature.

front_blocks.md: How does the peak wavelength of an object's emitted radiation change as its temperature increases?

back_blocks.md: The peak wavelength **decreases**, shifting to shorter wavelengths as the object's temperature increases.

cards.front_md: How does the peak wavelength of an object's emitted radiation change as its temperature increases?
cards.back_md: The peak wavelength **decreases**, shifting to shorter wavelengths as the object's temperature increases.

front_blocks.md: What real object provides the best approximation to an ideal black body?

back_blocks.md: **Stars** provide the best real-world approximation to an ideal black body.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A black body only absorbs radiation - it does not emit any.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
A perfect **black body** absorbs and emits all wavelengths of radiation; a good absorber is also a good emitter.

front_blocks.md: Define the **Stefan-Boltzmann Law**.

back_blocks.md: The **Stefan-Boltzmann Law** states that the total energy emitted by a black body per unit area per second is proportional to the fourth power of its absolute temperature.

cards.back_md: The **Stefan-Boltzmann Law** states that the total energy emitted by a black body per unit area per second is proportional to the fourth power of its absolute temperature.

front_blocks.md: State the Stefan-Boltzmann Law equation.

back_blocks.md: Where *L* is luminosity (W), *A* is surface area, *T* is absolute temperature (K), and σ is the **Stefan-Boltzmann constant**.

cards.back_md:
$L = σ A T^{4}$

Where *L* is luminosity (W), *A* is surface area, *T* is absolute temperature (K), and σ is the **Stefan-Boltzmann constant**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Doubling a star's surface temperature doubles its luminosity, assuming its surface area stays constant.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Luminosity is proportional to *T*<sup>4</sup>, so doubling the temperature increases luminosity by a factor of **16**, not 2.

front_blocks.md: Define **Wien's displacement law**.

back_blocks.md: **Wien's displacement law** states that the black body radiation curve for different temperatures peaks at a wavelength that is inversely proportional to the temperature.

cards.back_md: **Wien's displacement law** states that the black body radiation curve for different temperatures peaks at a wavelength that is inversely proportional to the temperature.

front_blocks.md: State Wien's Law equation.

back_blocks.md: $λ_{max} T = 2 . 9 \times 10^{-3} \text{m K}$

front_blocks.md: Why do hotter stars appear white or blue, while cooler stars appear red or yellow?

back_blocks.md: Hotter stars have their peak intensity at **shorter** wavelengths (blue/white end of the spectrum); cooler stars peak at **longer** wavelengths (red/yellow end).

front_blocks.md: What units must temperature be measured in when using Wien's Law?

back_blocks.md: **Kelvin** (K) - convert from degrees Celsius if the temperature is given in °C.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A star with a longer peak wavelength has a higher surface temperature than one with a shorter peak wavelength.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Peak wavelength is **inversely proportional** to temperature, so a longer peak wavelength means a **lower** surface temperature.
